official.deadline_note: Standing regulation: the deadline is 20 October of the academic year for which the scholarship is awarded. First-year students of first-cycle or long-cycle Master's studies who submit after 20 October are still granted the scholarship from the month of submission (no later than June), without compensation for previous months.
official.status_note: Official schedule for the 2026/2027 academic year published 28 August 2026: Rector's Scholarship applications are accepted from 1 to 20 October, with electronic submission only.
benefits: A form of financial support granted to students (including foreigners) in first-cycle, second-cycle and long-cycle Master's studies for outstanding academic performance, scientific, artistic or sports achievements
PLN 1,000 per month from October to June (9 months per academic year)
Awarded for one academic year (in principle for 9 months) and paid monthly to the student's bank account; paid twice a month, on the 15th and the last day of the month
Tax-exempt in Poland and not declared in the annual tax return
For first-year olympiad/sport laureates the number of scholarships is not limited, and the award can be combined with the scholarship from the Rector's Fund for Olympians
eligibility: Enrolled in first-cycle, second-cycle or long-cycle Master's studies at Jagiellonian University; foreign students admitted from the 2019/2020 academic year onward may apply regardless of citizenship or study terms

First year of first-cycle or long-cycle Master's studies: admitted in the year of the secondary school-leaving exam (matura) and a winner of an international olympiad or winner/finalist of a central-level olympiad, or a medalist in at least a Polish Championship-level sports competition

Higher years: outstanding academic performance, scientific or artistic achievements, or sports achievements at least at national level; awarded to the top 10% of students in a given programme/specialisation on a points score of grade average plus academic, artistic and sports achievements

First-year second-cycle (Master's) students may apply on the final-year results of the first-cycle studies on which their admission was based; two separate ranking lists are used (JU graduates by weighted GPA, graduates of other universities by arithmetic GPA, 10% awarded from each)

Not available to holders of a Master's degree (even if obtained abroad) or of a Bachelor's degree when re-enrolling in first-cycle studies, conditionally enrolled students, students who repeated a year (unless the next year was also completed), students resuming after removal from the student list, or applicants applying in the same year of study in which they were on leave in the previous academic year

Total entitlement period is 12 semesters: no more than 9 semesters on first-cycle and 7 on second-cycle studies, extended by 2 semesters for long-cycle Master's programmes lasting 11 or 12 semesters by law (Pharmacy, Medicine); part-time students may also apply, with full-time and part-time combined in one ranking list per year and programme
requirements: Applications must be submitted online only via the USOSweb system using the "Sign and submit electronically" function; there is no need to submit a printed version to the Scholarship Affairs Office
The application must be submitted by 20 October of the academic year for which the scholarship is awarded (2026/2027 round: 1-20 October 2026); the order of submissions does not matter
All achievements must be confirmed with an appropriate certificate attached electronically to the application in USOSweb; achievements reported after submission are not taken into account
The weighted grade point average must be calculated according to the Study Regulations and verified by the student's programme office in the USOS system
The scholarship holder must provide a bank account denominated in Polish zloty (PLN) with a bank operating in the territory of the Republic of Poland

Documents drawn up in a foreign language must be submitted with a translation into Polish (a regular translation for the rector's scholarship; a sworn translation is required only for the social scholarship)
documents: Certificates confirming each achievement cited in the application, attached electronically in USOSweb - electronic originals bearing an electronic signature or the authority's electronic seal, or a legible scan or photo for documents issued in paper form, with multi-page documents submitted as a single file containing all pages

For first-year second-cycle students who completed first-cycle studies at another university: a certificate confirming the arithmetic grade point average for the last year of first-cycle studies (the Bachelor's thesis defence grade is excluded)
selection_criteria: Applications are assessed using a points-based system: points for the grade average plus academic, artistic and sports achievements, cumulative within a category; the scholarship goes to the students with the highest number of points

A maximum of 10% of students in a given programme/specialisation; the pool is all students enrolled in that year of study as of 30 June of the previous academic year, including students repeating a year and those on leave (for first-year second-cycle students, those enrolled as of 15 October)

Only the achievements and grade average obtained in the previous academic year are evaluated; achievements from earlier years or from before the commencement of studies, including language certificates and school olympiad awards, are not taken into account

Ties are broken by: points for academic, artistic and sports achievements, then ECTS credits obtained, then the grade average over the entire course of studies, then (for first-year second-cycle students) the admission result
coverage: PLN 1,000 per month from October to June (9 months per academic year), paid by bank transfer
Paid to a bank account in Polish zloty (PLN) with a bank operating in the territory of the Republic of Poland; payments are made twice a month, on the 15th and the last day of the month
Tax-exempt in Poland and not declared in the annual tax return

A cash benefit paid in addition to study fees: under the published rules for students who began before 2019/2020, foreign students studying on a fee-paying basis may also receive the rector's scholarship - the award does not replace tuition
application_method: Go to the "For all" / "Common section" tab, then "Applications"
Choose the Rector's scholarship application and use the "sign and submit electronically" function, attaching the supporting documents
No printed version needs to be submitted to the Scholarship Affairs Office, by post, or to the University's electronic delivery address
official.application_route: One online application in USOSweb between 1 and 20 October 2026 ("For all" tab > Applications > Rector's scholarship), signed and submitted electronically with certificates attached
official.study_mode: Full-time and part-time (one common ranking list per year and programme/specialisation)
official.citizenship_residency: Open regardless of citizenship: foreign students admitted from the 2019/2020 academic year onward may receive the rector's scholarship regardless of citizenship or study terms; students who began before 2019/2020 qualify under the published rules for persons studying on the terms applicable to Polish citizens (e.g. permanent residence, long-term EU resident status, refugee or subsidiary protection, EU/EFTA worker status)
official.international_eligibility: Yes - a foreign student can receive the rector's scholarship, provided they started their studies in the academic year 2019/2020 or later
official.duration: One academic year, paid from October to June (in principle 9 months); in some academic years, by decision of the Rector, payment may be extended until July
official.description: The Rector's scholarship is a form of financial support granted to students (including foreigners) in first-cycle, second-cycle and long-cycle Master's studies for outstanding academic performance, scientific, artistic or sports achievements. It is awarded on the student's request for the academic year - in principle for 9 months, October to June - and paid monthly to a Polish zloty bank account held at a bank operating in Poland. The amount for a given academic year is determined by the Rector in agreement with the University Student Government Economic Committee.
official.program_type: Merit-based scholarship from the Jagiellonian University Scholarship Fund (stypendium rektora)

applicant_utility.summary: This is an in-study cash top-up for students already enrolled at Jagiellonian University: PLN 1,000 per month for October to June, paid into a Polish bank account, on top of whatever tuition you already pay - it does not fund your fees. First-years who arrived through an international or central-level olympiad or a Polish Championship medal have a near-automatic route with no numerical cap; everyone else competes for a 10%-per-programme quota scored on last year's grade average plus documented scientific, artistic or sports achievements. Everything hinges on one USOSweb form filed between 1 and 20 October, so the real preparation is hunting down achievement certificates and getting your weighted GPA verified before the window opens.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Enrolled JU students (including internationals admitted from 2019/2020 onward) with a strong previous-year grade average and certificates for scientific, artistic or sports achievements
application_readiness_checklist: In early October, log in to USOSweb and confirm the Rector's scholarship application is available under the "For all" / "Common section" tab and "Applications" before the 20th
Ask your programme office to verify your weighted grade average in USOS - the office's figure, not your own calculation, is the one ranked
Gather a certificate for every achievement you plan to claim well before 1 October; undocumented achievements score nothing
Prepare electronic originals bearing an electronic signature or the issuing authority's electronic seal (legible scans only for paper documents), merging multi-page certificates into one file
Arrange Polish translations for any foreign-language documents (a regular translation is enough for this scholarship)
Make sure you have a PLN account at a bank operating in Poland - payments cannot be sent elsewhere
Monitor USOSweb during assessment for a returned application and resubmit it with "Sign and submit electronically" after fixing what was requested
common_rejection_risks: Claiming achievements the regulations explicitly exclude - student organisation and academic club activity, organising conferences or workshops, language or competency certificates, unpublished papers still in review or in print, Rector's/Dean's awards, conference organisation grants - each scores zero and signals you misread the rules
A grade average below 4.0, or an average drawn from the wrong period: only the previous academic year counts, and earlier or pre-study achievements are ignored
Undocumented achievements - anything without an attached certificate is discarded, and achievements reported after submission are not considered
Missing the 20 October deadline; only the first-year olympiad route can survive it, and then payment starts from the month of application with no back-pay
Applying in the same year of study in which you were on leave in the previous academic year, or while conditionally enrolled - both bar the award outright
Holding the KPO scholarship at the same time, which forces full repayment of the rector's scholarship
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Tuition and any non-EU fee obligations, accommodation, health insurance, travel to Poland, and living costs for July-September unless the Rector extends payment into July in a given year
document_audit: Foreign-issued diplomas, transcripts and certificates need a Polish translation - sworn only for the social scholarship, a regular translation suffices for the rector's scholarship

First-year master's students who did their bachelor's at another university must attach a certificate of the arithmetic GPA for the final bachelor year with the thesis defence grade excluded; JU graduates are ranked on weighted GPA on a separate list, so check which list you land in
Multi-page certificates must be merged into a single file - separate uploads can be treated as incomplete

First-year olympiad and sport certificates must match the level stated in the regulations exactly (international olympiad winner, central-level olympiad winner or finalist, or at least Polish Championship medal), not a lower-tier competition
alerts: UJ reallocates the Scholarship Fund every autumn: PLN 1,000 per month is the latest officially published amount (2025/2026), and the figure for the 2026/2027 round appears in the News section around late October - re-check before budgeting
The 10% cap is per programme, specialisation and year of study, so your odds depend on your own cohort's strength, not on a university-wide average
If you study two programmes you may apply for each, but you can draw the scholarship from only one of them
The application window is short and fixed (1-20 October); USOSweb access problems must be solved through usosownia.uj.edu.pl before, not during, the deadline
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: One electronic application in USOSweb filed between 1 and 20 October and signed with "Sign and submit electronically", certificates attached; committees score the applications and decisions are paid twice monthly from October
